provenance: Lane split authored by Stage-2 decision-agent (read-only; returns JSON in reply), persisted by the orchestrator. All 48 IDs reconciled against intel/cti-pipeline.json (37 detection / 11 hunt) and verified in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — inbound attachment analysis, sandbox detonation of .hta/Office content, and user-reported-phish workflows make delivery detectable at the email perimeter
medium — inbound URL analysis, newly-registered / dynamic-DNS lookalike-domain detection, and secure-email-gateway link detonation make delivery observable at the perimeter
medium — anomalous-logon analytics (unusual source, impossible travel, dormant-account use) provide detection even when the credential itself is legitimate

medium — highly feasible identity detection: sign-ins from TOR/anomalous ASNs with a 'go-http-client' user agent, impossible-travel and off-hours-for-victim access are strong Entra ID sign-in-log signals

medium — highly feasible: distributed low-and-slow failed-auth patterns across many accounts, spikes of 4625/Entra sign-in failures from TOR ASNs, and a 'go-http-client' user agent are strong high-fidelity identity signals
medium — repeated failed authentications against externally facing services are detectable via authentication-failure analytics and lockout monitoring
medium — Outlook/Office spawning script or shell child processes, and the CVE-2017-11774 registry Home Page URL artifact, are detectable via process-lineage and registry monitoring
medium — web-proxy/DNS logs of clicks to dynamic-DNS/lookalike domains and browser-download telemetry provide detection
medium — mshta.exe executing remote/local .hta content and Office/macro child processes spawning script interpreters are detectable via process-creation and EDR telemetry
medium — PowerShell script-block/module logging, AMSI, and suspicious cmdlet sequences (encoded commands, download-and-invoke) are strong detections; obfuscation reduces static visibility

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — wscript/cscript/mshta executing script content that spawns command interpreters is detectable via process-creation telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Event Triggered Execution: Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — WMI-Activity operational logging and Sysmon EID 19/20/21 (WMI event filter/consumer/binding creation) provide reliable detection of this persistence

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — Run-key writes and Startup-folder drops are classic, well-covered autostart-monitoring detections (Sysmon EID 12/13)
medium — scheduled-task creation (Event ID 4698, Sysmon) with suspicious actions/paths is a reliable detection
medium — Entra ID audit logs of new device/service registrations, role assignments and credential additions are auditable identity-persistence signals
medium — anomalous privilege-elevation, exploit-driven process crashes/child spawns, and EDR exploit-guard telemetry provide detection, though 0-day can precede the first artifact
medium — a signed legitimate binary loading an unsigned/anomalous DLL from an unexpected path is detectable via image-load (Sysmon EID 7) and DLL-path anomaly analytics
medium — LSASS handle/process-access telemetry (Sysmon EID 10) and Credential Guard provide well-established detection
medium — registry access to SECURITY\Policy\Secrets and reg save of protected hives are detectable via registry and process auditing
medium — anomalous SYSVOL enumeration for Groups.xml/*.xml and Get-GPPPassword-style access are detectable via file-share access auditing and script-block logging
medium — access to credential-store files/APIs (Credential Manager, vaults) is detectable via file/API access telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — non-browser processes reading browser Login Data / credential SQLite stores are detectable via file-access and EDR telemetry
medium — bulk directory/role enumeration via Microsoft Graph / Azure AD Graph is visible in Entra ID audit and MSGraph activity logs; AzureHound produces a recognizable burst of read calls
medium — high-volume Resource Manager / Graph enumeration from a single identity is detectable via Azure activity and MSGraph audit logs

detection_candidates.technique_name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — creation of large/password-protected archives in staging directories by archive utilities is detectable via process-creation and file-creation telemetry
medium — anomalous internal RDP (Event ID 4624 type 10, unusual source-destination pairs, off-hours) is detectable via logon and network analytics
medium — beaconing patterns, anomalous user agents and connections to newly-seen/dynamic-DNS domains are detectable via proxy/DNS and network analytics, though content is often TLS-encrypted
medium — script hosts / LOLBins downloading executables from external hosts followed by execution are detectable via process-network correlation
medium — protocol-on-non-standard-port analytics (e.g. TLS/HTTP on unusual ports) provide detection

medium — installation/execution of AnyDesk (or other RMM) on hosts where it is not sanctioned, and its outbound connections, are detectable via software-inventory and network analytics (RMM allow-listing is a strong control)
medium — authentication and access from known TOR exit-node IPs (threat-intel-fed) is a strong, if noisy, signal; combined with the 'go-http-client' user agent it becomes high-fidelity

detection_candidates.technique_name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — large or unusual outbound transfers over protocols like FTP/HTTP to non-corporate destinations are detectable via network/DLP analytics

detection_candidates.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — security-tool stop/tamper events, and installation/loading of an unusual signed kernel disk driver, are detectable via EDR self-protection and driver-load (Sysmon EID 6) telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Clear Windows Event Logs
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — event-log clear events (Event ID 1102), wevtutil execution, and logging-continuity gaps are detectable via log-integrity monitoring
medium — mass file-overwrite/deletion behavior across many hosts in a short window is detectable via EDR ransomware/wiper behavior analytics and file-modification volume anomalies

medium — direct raw-disk write access from non-standard processes and simultaneous multi-host disk failures are detectable via kernel-driver-load and EDR behavior telemetry, though impact is immediate
medium — execution of vssadmin/wbadmin/bcdedit recovery-deletion commands and shadow-copy deletion are high-fidelity, well-covered detections when they occur pre-wipe

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — tool acquisition is off-victim; a hunt/threat-intel awareness item. Detection surface is on-victim execution of the acquired tools (see execution/discovery TTPs), not the acquisition itself

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — encryption/encoding defeats static inspection; hunt via entropy analysis and AMSI-visible decrypted content rather than a single signature
low — standard encoding blends with legitimate traffic; hunt via decoded content inspection and anomalous encoded-payload volume in web logs

hunting_candidates.technique_name: OS Credential Dumping: Cached Domain Credentials
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — cached-credential extraction is quiet on-host; hunt via registry/hive access and offline-cracking-precursor tooling execution
low — file-content credential searching resembles normal file access; hunt via mass file-read/enumeration patterns and access to known credential-file locations
low — passive sniffing generates little host telemetry; hunt via detection of promiscuous-mode enablement and sniffer-tool execution

low — forged SAML tokens produce sign-ins that look legitimate; hunt via AD FS token-signing-certificate access, sign-ins with no corresponding AD FS auth event, and unusual SAML token lifetimes/claims (a specialist detection, not a simple rule)

low — tunneled traffic is wrapped to look legitimate; hunt via volume/timing anomalies, unexpected long-lived outbound sessions and the presence of the EagleRelay binary rather than a network signature
low — encryption defeats content inspection; detection relies on behavioral beaconing and infrastructure indicators rather than payload signatures
low — by the time content-overwrite is observed the data is gone; hunt for the precursor driver load and abnormal direct-disk-write handle acquisition rather than the wipe itself
low — MBR overwrite manifests as unbootable systems; detection is limited to precursor driver-load and raw-write monitoring, so this is primarily a hunt/prevention (MBR write-protection) item
